previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for acute worsening of shortness of breath and chest discomfort following a missed dose of torsemide due to medication noncompliance during a period of housing instability. He presented with volume overload, weight gain, bibasilar crackles, and elevated BNP of 4403, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation. Treatment included aggressive IV diuresis with Lasix and metolazone, leading to improved symptoms and a discharge weight of 128.7 kg. His creatinine rose to 2.5 due to diuresis, prompting a temporary reduction in torsemide to every other day with plans to reassess based on renal function. He was started on spironolactone and continued on his baseline heart failure and diabetes medications. Psychiatry evaluated him for adjustment-related hopelessness but found no clinical depression. He declined right heart catheterization for volume assessment. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with close outpatient follow-up for medication titration, lab monitoring, and support for adherence and emotional well-being.

SUMMARY: ___ with sCHF (LVEF 20%, s/p ICD), CAD w/DES to ___

presented to the ED for eye swelling and hand rash, but was

exacerbation.

ACTIVE ISSUES

# Acute on Chronic Systolic Left Heart Failure
Patient found to be short of breath in the ED with pulmonary 
edema seen on CXR and proBNP elevated, consistent with his prior 
CHF exacerbations. Prior exacerbations have been attributed to 
dietary noncompliance and poor medication adherence, though he 
lives with family now to ""watch him."" He reports compliance with 
his medications, including torsemide, which he last took the 
morning of ___. On last admission (___), he was offered a 
right heart cath to determine volume status, but he declined. 
Weight on that discharge was 128.7kg. He is ___ on 
admission. Looking at prior records, he has been having slowly 
uptrending weight at clinic visits and via telehealth 
monitoring. He was treated for his exacerbation with furosemide 
drip at 20mg/hr with good urine output. However, the patient 
said that a very close ___ friend passed away and that 
he had to be at a funeral so he was discharged after only 2 days 
of IV diuresis. He received metolazone 5mg on the day of 
discharge to expedite diuresis. On discharge, his weight was 
131.6kg. He was instructed to continue on torsemide 140mg daily 
along with digoxin 0.0625 mg daily, isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg 
daily, hydralazine 20 mg Q8H, metoprolol succindate 75 mg daily, 
spironolactone 25 mg daily.

# Pruritus and Rash
Initially, there was concern for DRESS or Type I 
hypersensitivity in the ED. DRESS was thought unlikely given 
normal LFTs and lack of typical offending meds, and has been on 
medications for a long time. Has had signs of peripheral 
eosinophilia chronically, as high as 8.1% in ___. His face is 
symmetric on admission without puffiness. His hands remain dry 
and cracked, which was much improved after one day. He was iven 
hydroxyzine 25mg Q6H for pruritus.

# Eosinophilia
He has had chronic eosinophilia going back ___ years. There was 
low suspicion for malignancy. The trend of eosinophilia appeared 
to correspond with seasonal fluctuation, peaking between 
___ and ___.

# Hyperuricemia: Asymptomatic, therefore, no intervention was 
taken. The elevation likely caused by heart failure and kidney 
failure and unlikely to have long term effects on his health 
unless he becomes symptomatic.

CHRONIC ISSUES
# History of Ventricular Tachycardia: He had intermittent 
asymptomatic NSVT on recent admission, and EP interrogated ICD. 
No evidence of sustained VT was found and settings were left 
unchanged. Continued home amiodarone 200 mg BID, metoprolol XL 
75mg daily, and digoxin 0.0625mcg daily.
# Chronic Kidney Disease: Cr at recent baseline.
# Coronary Artery Disease: Continue home ASA, Plavix, 
atorvastatin, and metoprolol.
# Hypertension: Continue home meds as above  
# Hyperlipidemia: Continue home atorvastatin 80 mg.
# Type 2 diabetes: Continue on home insulin regimen of Lantus 55 
units qAM with added insulin sliding scale here.
# GERD: Continue home pantoprazole.

131.6kg.
- Continue torsemide 140mg PO daily.
